text:
Overall score: **6/10**. This is a small, readable codebase with decent tests and no obvious command injection or unsafe dependency surface. I would not call it production-ready yet because the ingest path can silently corrupt accounting data under realistic re-ingest scenarios, and validation/schema constraints are too loose for a tool that computes usage totals.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q` passes: **61 passed**. `git` is not installed here, so I could not inspect working-tree state.

**Issues**
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70): `70-84` high - Older same-rank records can overwrite newer records, so out-of-order RUNNING/RUNNING or terminal/terminal snapshots can regress elapsed/time data.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74): `74-80` high - “Unchanged” detection only compares `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec`, so changed CPU/GPU/user/partition/exit-code fields are skipped.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:40): `40-41` medium - Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal, which can block later updates from known nonterminal states.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:148): `148-162` high - Negative `AllocCPUS` and negative GPU counts are accepted, allowing negative CPU/GPU-hour reports.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:14): `14-25` medium - SQLite schema has no `CHECK` constraints for nonnegative CPU/GPU/elapsed values or nonblank text fields.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:152): `152-164` medium - Empty `User`, `Partition`, and `ExitCode` values are accepted despite being core reporting fields.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:123): `123-124` medium - Timestamps with offsets are preserved as text and later compared lexicographically, which can make date filtering wrong when mixed with naive or differently offset timestamps.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:65): `65,83,101,142` medium - Report filters compare timestamp strings in SQLite rather than normalized datetime values.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:52): `52-58` medium - `connect()` always creates and initializes the database, so report commands against a typo path silently create an empty DB.
- [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:122): `122,139,176` medium - Read-only report commands use the same database-creating path as ingest instead of failing on a missing DB.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13): `13-27` medium - Schema has no versioning or migration path, making future field/constraint changes risky for existing user databases.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:113): `113-121` low - `top` can fail if bad timestamp text already exists in the DB because `datetime.fromisoformat()` is called without defensive handling.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:167): `167-199` low - Ingest parses the full file into memory before database writes, which is avoidable for large `sacct` exports.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:58): `58-70,79-106,135-148` low - Reporting queries will full-scan the jobs table; there are no indexes for reference-time/grouping report paths.
- [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:13): `13-23` low - Test tooling is minimal and lacks lint/type/security checks, so several accepted-invalid-data paths are not caught automatically.

Estimated significant rewrite/change: **170 LOC**. That includes fixing upsert freshness semantics, adding parser/schema validation, separating create-vs-open DB flows, normalizing timestamp handling, adding schema versioning/indexes, and covering those behaviors in tests.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this as-is.**

issues.description: Older same-rank records can overwrite newer records and regress elapsed/time data.
Unchanged detection ignores CPU/GPU/user/partition/exit-code changes and can skip real updates.
Unknown Slurm states are treated as terminal and can block later lifecycle updates.
Negative CPU and GPU allocations are accepted and can produce negative usage reports.
Schema lacks CHECK constraints for nonnegative numeric values and nonblank required fields.
Empty User, Partition, and ExitCode values are accepted as valid records.
Offset-aware timestamps are stored as raw text without normalization, making later comparisons unreliable.
Report date filters rely on lexicographic text comparison instead of normalized datetime values.
Database connect always creates a DB, so read-only operations can silently create empty databases.
Report commands use the database-creating connection path and do not fail on missing DB files.
SQLite schema has no versioning or migration path for future changes.
Top-users report can crash if invalid timestamp text already exists in the database.
Parser materializes the entire input file before database writes, which does not scale to large dumps.
Reporting queries have no supporting indexes and will full-scan the jobs table.
Project lacks lint/type/security tooling, leaving validation bugs to manual review.
